cards.alt: Sample multiple choice card: Which cell type most likely stays in G0 for life?

questions.stem: A flow cytometry histogram of a growing culture shows two peaks, at 2C and 4C. Cells in the 4C peak are in:
questions.explanation: Cells at 4C have replicated their DNA but not yet divided, so they are in G2 or M. G1 and G0 cells have 2C, and cells in early S phase lie between the two peaks.

questions.stem: A tumor has a mutation that prevents Rb from binding E2F. The most likely effect is:
options: Continuous expression of S phase genes
questions.explanation: Without Rb-E2F binding, E2F is free and S phase genes are active regardless of growth signals. This removes a brake, so arrest is not expected, and the mutation does not directly involve p53 or telomerase.
questions.subtopic: Cancer and loss of cell cycle control

questions.stem: Mitochondrial DNA is maternally inherited mainly because:
options: The egg destroys its own mitochondria
Sperm mitochondria are degraded in the zygote
questions.explanation: Sperm have mitochondria in the midpiece, but they are degraded in the zygote. The egg keeps its own. Sperm mitochondria do exist and function.

questions.stem: Which pair of tissues derives from neural crest?
questions.explanation: Neural crest forms melanocytes, adrenal medulla, Schwann cells and sensory and autonomic neurons. Hepatocytes and pancreatic cells are endoderm, muscle and bone are mesoderm, and the lens and retina arise from surface ectoderm and neuroectoderm.

questions.stem: Embryos lacking maternal bicoid mRNA will most likely lack:
options: Hox gene expression in all segments
questions.explanation: Bicoid is an anterior morphogen, so loss gives embryos missing head and thorax. Posterior structures depend on other maternal factors. Neural crest is not tested, and Hox genes in the abdomen are still expressed.

demo_cards.back: The cell finishes growing, checks the replicated DNA, and makes proteins needed for mitosis such as tubulin and cyclin B.

demo_cards.text: Order of the cell cycle: {{c1::G1}}, then {{c2::S}}, then {{c3::G2}}, then {{c4::M}}.
demo_cards.extra: G1, S and G2 together are interphase.

demo_cards.stem: Which cell type most likely stays in G0 for life?
demo_cards.why: Mature neurons are terminally differentiated and do not divide. The other three populations keep cycling to replace lost cells.
DNA doubles in S phase. Mitosis only divides the already doubled DNA between two daughter cells.
